statement.p: Let \int_{0}^2 f(x) \, dx = 7, \quad \int_{0}^3 f(x) \, dx = 3, \quad \int_{0}^2 g(x) \, dx = 11, \quad \int_{2}^3 g(x) \, dx = -13, \quad
Use these values to evaluate the given definite integrals.
d) Find the value a such that \displaystyle \int_{0}^3 \left(a f(x) + g(x)\right) \, dx = 0.

static.solution:
Solution:
a) \int_0^2 \left(f(x) + g(x)\right) \, dx = \int_0^2 f(x) \, dx + \int_0^2 g(x) \, dx = 7 + 11 = 18.
b) First find the integral of g from 0 to 3. \int_0^3 g(x) \, dx = \int_0^2 g(x) \, dx + \int_2^3 g(x) \, dx = 11 - 13 = -2. Then \int_0^3 \left(f(x) - g(x)\right) \, dx = \int_0^3 f(x) \, dx - \int_0^3 g(x) \, dx = 3 + 2 = 5.
c) First find the integral of f from 2 to 3. \begin{array}{rcl} \displaystyle\int_0^3 f(x) \, dx \amp =\amp \displaystyle\int_0^2 f(x) \, dx + \int_2^3 f(x) \, dx \\ 3 \amp =\amp 7 + \displaystyle\int_2^3 f(x) \, dx \\ \displaystyle\int_2^3 f(x) \, dx \amp =\amp -4 \end{array} Then \int_{2}^3 \left(3f(x) + 2g(x)\right) \, dx = 3\int_{2}^3 f(x) \, dx + 2\int_{2}^3 g(x) \, dx = 3(-4) + 2(-13) = -38.
d) Substitute known values for the integrals. \begin{array}{rcl} \displaystyle \int_{0}^3 \left(a f(x) + g(x)\right) \, dx \amp =\amp 0 \\ a \displaystyle \int_0^3 f(x) \, dx + \int_0^3 g(x) \, dx \amp =\amp 0\\ a(3) - 2 \amp =\amp \\ a \amp =\amp \frac{ + 2}{3} \end{array}
